rationale: Both legs are individually known anomalies (net stock issuance; intangible/goodwill growth), but the specific soft-asset-expansion × equity-dilution interaction is not in the archive and is economically coherent with a consistent negative sign — though the RANK of Δ(intan+gdwl)/at will be dominated by mass-at-zero ties for the many firms with no reported intangibles, which risks degenerate ranks and thin effective coverage.

Lagging the financing leg is a substantive (not cosmetic) fix to the mechanical contemporaneous capex–financing link in the archived "Dilutive Capex Shock"/"External-Funding Share" signals, and the expression matches the stated ordering hypothesis, but it remains structurally close to those prior signals so the incremental information content is uncertain.

GROWTH(csho) is unadjusted share-count growth, so the "dilution" leg is mechanically contaminated by splits and stock dividends (which are not dilution) while otherwise being a direct rediscovery of the Pontiff–Woodgate net share issuance anomaly crossed with the PPE/asset-growth anomaly.

The labor-expansion leg adds genuinely new content (hiring-rate anomaly interacted with net debt issuance rather than another balance-sheet asset-growth proxy), but the structure is nearly identical to the archived "Debt-Funded Tangible Capacity Expansion," so it should be judged on whether emp growth adds incremental power beyond the already-tested tangible version.

Δlt/at is close to an accounting-identity restatement of asset growth and is mechanically co-determined with an inventory build (inventory must be funded), so the product largely re-expresses the asset-growth/inventory-growth anomalies and substantially overlaps the archived "Debt-Funded Tangible Capacity Expansion," which already paired inventory growth with net debt issuance.

The financing leg is simply the negation of the archived "External-Funding Share of Capex" measure (net external financing) with dividends folded in, making this a sign-mirrored variant of an already-tested signal and a rediscovery of the well-documented total-external-financing/net-payout anomaly rather than a new mechanism.
